description: Cloud Village focuses on cloud security, container escapes, Kubernetes hardening, AWS and Azure exploitation, multi-cloud IAM toxic combinations, and CaaS runtime analysis.

talks.title: Workshop: Kubernetes Security 101 Best Practices
talks.teaser: Magno Logan delivers a comprehensive workshop on securing Kubernetes clusters, covering API servers, etcd, RBAC, admission controllers, and network policies.
talks.summary:
Foundations of Kubernetes Cluster Architecture

Securing production Kubernetes clusters requires deep understanding of control plane components—including the API server, etcd datastore, kubelet daemons, and worker nodes.

Hardening Managed and Self-Hosted Clusters

Magno Logan explores configuration best practices across major cloud managed offerings (EKS, GKE, AKS) and bare-metal deployments.

Implementing Robust RBAC and Admission Controllers

Logan demonstrates how to configure Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with least privilege and deploy Open Policy Agent (OPA) Gatekeeper admission controllers.

Container Runtime Security and Network Segmentation

The workshop provides actionable blueprints for securing pod-to-pod communications via CNI network policies and enforcing immutable container runtimes.

talks.title: Attack Vectors for APIs with AWS API Gateway Lambda Authorizers
talks.teaser: Alexandre Sieira breaks down common implementation pitfalls and bypasses in AWS API Gateway custom Lambda authorizers.
talks.summary:
The Shift to Serverless APIs on AWS

Modern cloud applications leverage serverless architectures (AWS SAM, Serverless Framework) combining Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda to process API requests at scale.

Deconstructing Custom Lambda Authorizers

Alexandre Sieira examines how Lambda authorizers validate bearer tokens, generate IAM policy documents, and cache authorization decisions for downstream routes.

Exploiting IAM Policy Caching Flaws

Sieira reveals critical vulnerabilities where flawed authorizer logic generates wildcard IAM resource policies or improperly keys policy caches, allowing unauthorized cross-tenant API access.

Hardening Serverless API Authorizers

The author provides developers with secure reference implementations and testing harnesses to validate Lambda authorization logic.

talks.title: Attack Vectors on Terraform Environments
talks.teaser: Mazin Ahmed exposes attack vectors targeting Terraform Infrastructure-as-Code environments, extracting plaintext secrets from state files and CI/CD pipelines.
talks.summary:
The Proliferation of Infrastructure-as-Code

Terraform has become the industry standard for provisioning multi-cloud infrastructure, managing foundational cloud networks, IAM roles, and databases.

Exploiting Exposed Terraform State Files

Mazin Ahmed demonstrates how unencrypted or improperly permissioned terraform.tfstate files leak plaintext cloud credentials, database passwords, and TLS private keys.

Pivoting Through CI/CD and Remote Backends

Ahmed details exploitation techniques targeting Terraform Cloud, GitHub Actions, and Jenkins pipelines to inject malicious resource blocks and escalate cloud privileges.

Securing Infrastructure-as-Code Pipelines

The author provides organizations with state file encryption standards, pre-commit static analysis tools (Checkov, tfsec), and least-privilege IAM deployment models.

talks.title: AWS Cloud Attack Vectors and Security Controls
talks.teaser: Kavisha Sheth reviews top AWS cloud attack vectors, mapping adversary techniques to defensive detection rules and IAM governance controls.
talks.summary:
The Expanding Enterprise Attack Surface in AWS

As organizations migrate legacy workloads to AWS, complex cloud-native architectures introduce misconfigurations and permission creep across cloud services.

Analyzing Common AWS Exploitation Chains

Kavisha Sheth analyzes real-world attack vectors, including SSRF against the EC2 Instance Metadata Service (IMDSv1), permissive S3 bucket policies, and unauthenticated Lambda triggers.

Implementing Cloud-Native Detective and Preventive Controls

Sheth maps offensive vectors directly to AWS security services—including AWS GuardDuty, Security Hub, AWS Config rules, and IAM Access Analyzer.

A Pragmatic Blueprint for Cloud Posture Hardening

The presentation provides cloud architects with a prioritized hardening checklist to enforce MFA, disable legacy metadata endpoints, and establish least-privilege IAM policies.

talks.title: Azure Active Directory Hacking Wars
talks.teaser: Batuhan Sancak demonstrates advanced attack techniques targeting Azure Active Directory, including Primary Refresh Token (PRT) theft and OAuth abuse.
talks.summary:
The Ubiquity of Azure Active Directory in Enterprise Identity

With over 15 million enterprise tenants and adoption across 95% of Fortune 500 companies, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) is the primary target for identity-driven attacks.

Extracting Primary Refresh Tokens (PRT) for Seamless Auth

Batuhan Sancak demonstrates extracting Azure AD Primary Refresh Tokens (PRTs) from memory and TPM-backed device registrations to bypass multi-factor authentication.

Abusing Service Principals and Illicit Consent Grants

Sancak walks through compromising high-privilege service principals, injecting malicious OAuth app credentials, and moving laterally across linked Microsoft 365 tenants.

Defending Azure AD Identity Environments

The author outlines conditional access policies, continuous access evaluation (CAE), and Azure AD Identity Protection monitoring to intercept credential replay attacks.

talks.title: Cloud Security Orienteering: Navigating Legacy & Multi-Cloud Chaos
talks.teaser: Rami McCarthy shares a pragmatic guide for newly hired security engineers to rapidly orient, map, and prioritize risk in sprawling, messy multi-cloud estates.
talks.summary:
The Reality of Messy Enterprise Cloud Environments

Few security professionals inherit pristine, greenfield cloud architectures; most must secure sprawling multi-account environments filled with technical debt and orphaned assets.

Rapid Reconnaissance and Asset Mapping

Rami McCarthy introduces 'Cloud Security Orienteering', a structured methodology to quickly discover account hierarchies, IAM boundaries, and internet-facing egress points.

Prioritizing High-Impact Vulnerabilities Over Alert Noise

McCarthy explains how to cut through thousands of CSPM alerts to focus on toxic risk combinations—such as public buckets linked to overprivileged service accounts.

A 30-60-90 Day Roadmap for Cloud Security Leads

The presentation provides actionable guidance for building relationships with DevOps teams, establishing automated baseline guardrails, and driving remediation.

talks.title: CSPM2CloudTrail: Extending CSPM Tools with Threat Hunting Context
talks.teaser: Rodrigo Montoro introduces CSPM2CloudTrail, bridging static Cloud Security Posture Management misconfigurations with dynamic AWS CloudTrail event analysis.
talks.summary:
The Limitations of Static CSPM and Noisy CloudTrail Logs

While Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) tools flag static misconfigurations, AWS CloudTrail logs thousands of API calls per minute without contextual prioritization.

Introducing CSPM2CloudTrail for Contextual Threat Hunting

Rodrigo Montoro presents CSPM2CloudTrail, an open-source tool that enriches static posture findings with dynamic CloudTrail API telemetry.

Detecting Active Exploitation of Misconfigured Assets

By correlating high-risk configurations (e.g. public security groups) with specific CloudTrail event histories, defenders identify whether assets were actively probed or exploited.

Automating Cloud Incident Response Triage

Montoro demonstrates how SOC analysts can accelerate triage workflows by automatically isolating compromised IAM credentials and generating remediation timelines.

talks.title: Detection Challenges in Cloud-Connected Credential Attacks
talks.teaser: Rod Soto explores the telemetry gaps and detection challenges facing defenders when threat actors abuse SSO and cloud credentials across hybrid perimeters.
talks.summary:
The Blurring Perimeter in Cloud-Connected Enterprises

As enterprise identities span on-premises directories and SaaS applications, traditional network perimeters dissolve into distributed identity exchanges.

Dissecting Cloud Credential Access and Replay Attacks

Rod Soto examines advanced credential attacks—including session cookie hijacking, federated SAML token forging, and cloud API key exfiltration.

Telemetry Blindspots in Cloud Audit Logging

Soto details common visibility gaps across cloud provider logs, illustrating how adversaries evade detection by throttling API calls and leveraging legitimate management consoles.

Designing Resilient Identity Detection Pipelines

The author provides behavioral detection rules (Sigma, Splunk queries) to detect impossible travel, anomalous user-agent strings, and sudden IAM policy modifications.

talks.title: Exploiting the O365 Duo 2FA Misconfiguration
talks.teaser: Cassandra Young demonstrates a misconfiguration in Microsoft 365 Duo 2FA implementations that allows mobile email clients to bypass two-factor prompts.
talks.summary:
The Mechanics of Multi-Factor Authentication in Office 365

Organizations frequently integrate third-party identity providers (such as Cisco Duo) with Microsoft 365 to enforce multi-factor authentication across enterprise mailboxes.

Discovering the Mobile Client Authentication Loophole

Cassandra Young reveals how incomplete conditional access rules and legacy ActiveSync / basic authentication protocols create an authentication bypass.

Executing 2FA Bypasses on Mobile Endpoints

By spoofing specific mobile user-agent headers and basic authentication endpoints, an attacker with stolen credentials authenticates directly to Exchange Online without triggering Duo prompts.

Remediating Duo and Azure Conditional Access Policies

Young provides administrators with step-by-step conditional access configurations to enforce modern authentication and block legacy protocol bypasses.

talks.title: Extracting All the Azure Passwords: MicroBurst & Cloud Recon
talks.teaser: NetSPI researcher Karl Fosaaen demonstrates automated Azure post-exploitation with MicroBurst, dumping credentials from Automation Accounts and Key Vaults.
talks.summary:
The Expanding Attack Surface in Microsoft Azure

As enterprises migrate mission-critical applications to Azure, developers often leave administrative credentials and API keys stored across distributed cloud services.

Automating Azure Reconnaissance with MicroBurst

Karl Fosaaen introduces updates to MicroBurst, a PowerShell toolkit designed for automated Azure subscription enumeration, privilege escalation, and credential discovery.

Dumping Secrets Across Azure Services

Fosaaen demonstrates extracting plaintext passwords from Azure Automation Runbooks, Key Vaults, App Service configuration strings, and Virtual Machine user-data scripts.

Securing Azure Credentials with Managed Identities

The author advises cloud architects on migrating away from hardcoded secrets by implementing Azure Managed Identities and strict RBAC on Key Vaults.

talks.title: Hunting for AWS Exposed Resources: S3, RDS, & SQS
talks.teaser: Felipe Pr0teus shares automated OSINT and scanning techniques to discover exposed AWS cloud assets, including public RDS database snapshots and SQS queues.
talks.summary:
The Global Epidemic of Publicly Exposed Cloud Assets

AWS allows users to make resources publicly accessible by design, but configuration oversights frequently expose private enterprise databases, queues, and object stores to the internet.

Scanning Beyond S3 Buckets

Felipe Pr0teus explores hunting methodologies targeting less-monitored AWS services—including public Amazon RDS database snapshots, exposed SQS message queues, and unauthenticated Lambda function URLs.

Automating Attack Surface Discovery

Pr0teus demonstrates custom reconnaissance scripts that query public AWS resource APIs and parse DNS certificate transparency logs to identify corporate asset exposures.

Implementing Automated Cloud Guardrails

The author provides AWS IAM and SCP (Service Control Policy) templates to permanently block public resource sharing across enterprise AWS organizations.

talks.title: I Know Who Has Access to My Cloud, Do You? Continuous IAM Governance
talks.teaser: Igal Flegmann explores Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM), demonstrating how to continuously monitor effective permissions across multi-cloud.
talks.summary:
The Inevitability of Cloud Breaches

While robust security practices (passwordless identity, conditional access) stop the majority of attacks, complex multi-cloud environments inevitably suffer identity compromise.

The Permissions Explosion Across Cloud Providers

Igal Flegmann analyzes the challenge of calculating 'effective permissions' across interconnected roles, groups, assume-role policies, and service principals.

Continuous Monitoring and Anomaly Detection

Flegmann demonstrates how Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM) platforms analyze real-time API call telemetry against assigned permissions to detect privilege misuse.

Achieving True Least-Privilege IAM

The presentation provides cloud teams with automated workflows to continuously right-size unused IAM permissions and eliminate dangerous privilege escalation paths.

talks.title: Identifying Toxic Combinations of Permissions in Multi-Cloud
talks.teaser: Michael Raggo examines toxic combinations across 24,000 cloud permissions in AWS, Azure, and GCP, mapping privilege escalation graphs.
talks.summary:
The Sprawl of 24,000 Multi-Cloud Permissions

With over 10,000 permissions in AWS and thousands more in Azure and GCP, enterprise IAM architectures contain vast matrices of overlapping authorization rules.

Defining Toxic Permission Combinations

Michael Raggo explains how two individually benign permissions (such as iam:CreatePolicyVersion and iam:SetDefaultPolicyVersion) combine into lethal privilege escalation vectors.

Graph-Based Analysis of Cloud Attack Paths

Raggo demonstrates graph modeling techniques that map non-linear attack pathways from unprivileged developer identities to full cloud organization admin.

Automated Detection and Least-Privilege Remediation

The author presents automated policy analysis tools to audit IAM policy documents and eliminate dangerous permission pairings across multi-cloud environments.

talks.title: Kubernetes Goat: Hands-On Kubernetes Security Learning
talks.teaser: Madhu Akula introduces Kubernetes Goat, an open-source vulnerable-by-design Kubernetes cluster environment for hands-on offensive and defensive learning.
talks.summary:
The Need for Hands-On Container Security Education

Securing containerized workloads running on Kubernetes requires practical experience exploiting real-world misconfigurations and container runtime flaws.

Architecture of the Kubernetes Goat Testbed

Madhu Akula presents Kubernetes Goat, a vulnerable-by-design environment engineered to simulate complex multi-tier container security vulnerabilities.

Exploring Real-World Kubernetes Attack Scenarios

Akula walks through live challenge scenarios—including container breakouts via privileged mounts, SSRF targeting the cloud metadata API, and exploiting RBAC misconfigurations.

Defensive Verification and Runtime Hardening

The author illustrates how defenders can use the platform to validate Falco runtime detection rules, OPA policies, and container scanning tools.

talks.title: Onions in the Cloud Make the CISO Proud: Security Onion Cloud Deployments
talks.teaser: Security Onion lead Wes Lambert demonstrates deploying distributed network security monitoring (NSM) and threat hunting sensors in AWS and Azure.
talks.summary:
The Cloud Visibility Gap for Enterprise Defenders

While over 90% of enterprises utilize cloud services, defenders frequently lack visibility into east-west inter-instance traffic and egress data flows.

Deploying Security Onion in Hybrid and Multi-Cloud

Wes Lambert demonstrates architecting distributed Security Onion 2 clusters natively inside AWS and Microsoft Azure virtual networks.

Capturing Cloud Network Traffic via VPC Mirroring

Lambert explains how to leverage native cloud packet mirroring (AWS VPC Traffic Mirroring and Azure Virtual Network TAP) to feed Zeek and Suricata sensors.

Hunting Cloud Threats with Centralized Analytics

The presentation showcases threat hunting workflows across aggregated cloud network logs, full packet captures, and host telemetry in the Security Onion console.

talks.title: Cloud Village Opening Note
talks.teaser: Jayesh Singh Chauhan welcomes attendees to DEF CON 29 Cloud Village, introducing the speaker lineup, cloud CTF challenges, and community workshops.
talks.summary:
In this opening address at the DEF CON 29 Cloud Village, village founder Jayesh Singh Chauhan welcomes attendees and kicks off the third annual gathering dedicated to cloud security research, offensive operations, and defensive architecture. He begins at 01:00 by reflecting on the benefits of the hybrid virtual conference format, which enables thousands of global security practitioners to participate simultaneously without geographic barriers.

Jayesh announces the kickoff of the Cloud Village CTF at 02:00, detailing the registration steps and portal access for the multi-cloud competition. At 03:00, he reviews event guidelines, the community code of conduct, and moderation policies across the official communication platforms. He walks through the CTF portal structure at 04:00, highlighting challenges across major public cloud providers including Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) at 05:00.

Highlighting community engagement at 06:00, Jayesh invites attendees to collaborate in real time on the DEF CON Discord channels and Twitter. He previews the weekend schedule at 08:00, highlighting hands-on tool demonstrations, technical briefings, and fast-paced lightning talks. He concludes at 09:00 by expressing heartfelt appreciation to the volunteer speaker operations team, CTF authors, and global attendees who make the Cloud Village possible. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: PK-WHY: Demystifying Public Key Infrastructure in Cloud Architectures
talks.teaser: Kevin Chen breaks down Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) concepts, removing the intimidation around TLS certificates, trust chains, and cloud CAs.
talks.summary:
The Intimidation Factor of Public Key Infrastructure

Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and X.509 certificates form the cryptographic backbone of cloud communications, yet developers and security engineers often avoid auditing them.

Demystifying Certificates and Trust Chains

Kevin Chen explains the fundamentals of asymmetric key generation, Certificate Authorities (CAs), root trust stores, and intermediate certificate validation.

Common PKI Implementation Pitfalls in Cloud Systems

Chen reviews common operational mistakes—such as hardcoded private keys, disabled certificate verification, and improper wildcards in cloud load balancers.

Modern Automated Certificate Management

The author demonstrates using automated protocols (ACME, AWS Certificate Manager, HashiCorp Vault) to eliminate manual certificate rotations and manage mTLS securely.

talks.title: Understanding Google Cloud Misconfiguration Using GCP Goat
talks.teaser: Joshua presents GCP Goat, an intentionally vulnerable Google Cloud Platform testbed for learning IAM privilege escalation and cloud storage exploitation.
talks.summary:
The Rising Adoption and Attack Surface of Google Cloud

As enterprises scale workloads on Google Cloud Platform (GCP), security teams must understand the distinct IAM and service architecture that differentiates GCP from AWS and Azure.

Introducing the GCP Goat Vulnerable Environment

Joshua demonstrates GCP Goat, an open-source testbed featuring intentionally misconfigured GCP services for hands-on security training.

Exploiting GCP IAM and Storage Misconfigurations

The author walks through multi-stage attack scenarios, demonstrating Cloud Storage bucket enumeration, Service Account token impersonation, and Cloud Function privilege escalation.

Hardening GCP Deployments and Enforcing Guardrails

Joshua provides cloud administrators with Organization Policy constraints, VPC Service Controls, and IAM condition configurations to secure GCP environments.

talks.title: Using Barq to Perform AWS Post-Exploitation
talks.teaser: Mohammed Aldoub presents Barq, an AWS post-exploitation framework that automates attacking live EC2 instances and dumping SSM Parameter Store secrets.
talks.summary:
The Need for Automated AWS Post-Exploitation Frameworks

Once initial AWS credentials are compromised, red team operators require specialized tooling to enumerate assets, extract secrets, and pivot across cloud instances.

Introducing the Barq Post-Exploitation Toolkit

Mohammed Aldoub introduces Barq, an open-source offensive framework designed to execute automated attacks against running AWS infrastructure.

Attacking EC2 Instances Without SSH Keys

Aldoub demonstrates how Barq abuses AWS Systems Manager (SSM) and EC2 user-data scripts to execute root shellcode on running instances without requiring SSH keypairs.

Automated Secret Extraction and Defense Mitigations

The author showcases dumping stored AWS Secrets Manager and SSM Parameters, concluding with defensive IAM policies to restrict SSM Agent abuse.

talks.title: WhoC: Peeking Under the Hood of Container-as-a-Service Offerings
talks.teaser: Palo Alto Networks researcher Yuval Avrahami presents WhoC, a container image tool that extracts the underlying container runtime in public CaaS clouds.
talks.summary:
The Black-Box Trust Model in Containers-as-a-Service (CaaS)

Enterprises deploy business-critical applications on multi-tenant CaaS platforms (like AWS Fargate and Azure Container Instances), trusting providers to enforce strict workload isolation.

Introducing WhoC: Container Runtime Extraction

Yuval Avrahami presents WhoC, an open-source container image designed to extract the underlying container engine binary running on host infrastructure.

Exploiting File Descriptor Leaks During Container Initialization

Avrahami explains how WhoC exploits subtle race conditions and leaked file descriptors in container runtimes (such as runc) to inspect host-level execution environments.

Auditing Public Cloud CaaS Security Boundaries

The author shares research findings across major cloud providers, highlighting how runtime transparency helps researchers identify container escape zero-days.

talks.title: Windows Server Containers Are Broken
talks.teaser: Daniel Prizmant demonstrates fundamental architectural security flaws in Windows Server Process-Isolated Containers, executing root container escapes.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of Windows Server Containers

Unlike Linux containers that rely on cgroups and namespaces, Windows Server containers implement process isolation by partitioning the Windows NT kernel and object manager.

Auditing Windows Process-Isolated Containers

Daniel Prizmant analyzes the security boundary of Windows Server containers, evaluating whether process-isolated containers represent a secure multi-tenant boundary.

Discovering Multiple Kernel-Level Container Escapes

Prizmant demonstrates multiple novel container escape vectors—including named pipe impersonation, CSRSS memory corruption, and kernel object sharing—to break out to the host OS.

Recommendations for Secure Windows Containerization

The author advises cloud operators to mandate Hyper-V isolation (virtualized containers) for multi-tenant Windows workloads to prevent kernel-level host compromise.
